subject: Onboarding evaluation artifacts + action register — load & latency validation
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Rios <daniel.rios@quikcart.com>, Ops Team <ops@quikcart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding evaluation artifacts + action register — load & latency validation

Hi Daniel / QuikCart Ops team,

Great to meet you during yesterday's walkthrough. Per our onboarding checklist, this thread will capture the load/latency validation plan, the artifacts we expect to exchange, and the action register for the first run. High level goals we agreed:

- Target P95 latency <= 120ms for single-request text generation at 64 tokens (baseline model).
- Sustained throughput target: 600 concurrent requests with 95th percentile tail <= 200ms under steady-state traffic pattern.
- Spike test: 1-minute bursts up to 1,200 RPS to validate graceful degradation/fallback.

Action items I put on the register below (please confirm owners and times):
1) QuikCart to provide representative traffic CSV + sample prompts (Ops) — due Wed 14 Apr EOD.
2) Redwood to run baseline load script in our preprod with QuikCart prefix cache enabled and share raw telemetry (Redwood SRE / Karthik) — run 12 Apr 10:00 PT.
3) Joint verification call to review results and discuss quantization/upper-bound workarounds (Vanessa / Monica / QuikCart Ops) — 14 Apr 11:00 PT.

I attached a simple load plan template (qc-loadplan-v1.xlsx) and a Redwood starter loadscript (redwood-loadscript-20270412.json) we'll use as the baseline. When you send over the sample prompts, include an indication of the request-size distribution (short/medium/long) and any sticky-session routing we should emulate.

Also, quick note on artifacts we will upload to the shared Drive folder: raw traces (JSON), aggregated token-cost breakdown, and a short runbook that lists the fallback policies exercised.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

From: Daniel Rios <daniel.rios@quikcart.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ops Team <ops@quikcart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding evaluation artifacts + action register — load & latency validation

Vanessa — thanks for the clear plan. Ops here. Quick answers and confirmations: 

- We'll deliver the sample prompts + traffic distribution by EOD today (12 Apr). Expect two CSVs: live-sample-1.csv and synthetic-mix.csv.
- For the spike test: we can schedule the 1,200 RPS window on 14 Apr at 11:00 PT if that still works with Redwood's joint verification slot.
- We use sticky-user routing for sessionAffinity=true on some checkout endpoints — we'll mark those examples in the CSVs.

Small ask: can Redwood include a short checklist that tells our infra team what versioned model (name + quantization) you plan to run and the expected GPU footprint for the baseline run? That will help us ensure capacity is available.

Attaching the first pass of the traffic CSVs in the Drive link (I'll upload after this mail).

— Daniel
Daniel Rios
Head of Ops, QuikCart Inc.
ops@quikcart.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Daniel Rios <daniel.rios@quikcart.com>, Ops Team <ops@quikcart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding evaluation artifacts + action register — load & latency validation

Thanks Daniel — got the CSV preview in Drive. Quick technical notes and the runbook outline I will execute during the 12 Apr baseline (confirming time: 12 Apr 10:00 PT, per Vanessa):

Planned baseline configuration:
- Model: redwood/gpt-mid-2027 (fp16), fallback variant: redwood/gpt-mid-2027-q4 (quantized for cost sim).
- Batching: dynamic continuous batching with max_batch_size=64; target batch window=10ms.
- Cache: prefix KV caching enabled for repeated customer prompts (we'll parameterize cache-hit ratio from your CSV).
- GPU footprint estimate: 3x A100 equivalent slots for sustained 600 concurrent requests at ~64-token responses (we'll send exact telemetry after run).

Load script notes (attached redwood-loadscript-20270412.json):
- Run 1: steady-state profile with mixed short/medium/long from synthetic-mix.csv for 20 minutes. Collect p50/p90/p95/p99 latency.
- Run 2: ramp from 600 -> 1200 RPS in 5 minutes to exercise autoscaler. Track token-drop and fallback invocations.
- Run 3: spike test (60s at 1200 RPS) followed by 10-minute cooldown to observe recovery behavior and tail latencies.

I will produce an artifacts package after the run: aggregated latencies CSV, raw trace JSON, model-cost-per-token.csv, and a short notes.md describing any retry/fallback events. Upload target: shared Drive folder.

If QuikCart wants, we can also run an alternate baseline with quantized variant to show cost/latency delta — that would be an add-on 30-min test.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Ops Team <sre@quikcart.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Daniel Rios <daniel.rios@quikcart.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding evaluation artifacts + action register — load & latency validation

Thanks team — we executed the scheduled runs this morning (14 Apr 11:00 PT). Summary and artifacts attached to the Drive folder: qc-test-results-20270414.csv (aggregated metrics), traces/raw-20270414.json (raw traces), and a short notes doc. Key observations: 

- Steady-state (20m): P95 latency = 118ms, P99 = 265ms. Token cost line-item attached.
- Ramp test to 1,200 RPS: autoscaler kicked at 7m30s; we observed ~8% increased tail latency during the add capacity window. No request loss.
- 60s spike at 1,200 RPS: one fallback policy triggered (model-variant fallback to q4) for ~45s; recovery to baseline within 90s.

Questions / next steps:
- Can Redwood provide the exact telemetry slice that maps fallback invocations to request IDs so we can correlate with our internal logs?
- We'd like a short follow-up call to review P99 behavior and explore a tuning plan (adjust batch window and autoscale thresholds). Proposed: 15 Apr 09:00 PT.

We'll mark action items as closed for the CSV delivery and will wait for Redwood's telemetry upload.

— QuikCart SRE (on behalf of Ops)
SRE Team | QuikCart Inc.
sre@quikcart.com
